html:
The Cucuteni-Trypillia culture was a farming culture of the Neolithic and Copper Age in today's Ukraine, Moldova and Romania, from about 5500 to 2750 BCE, known for painted pottery and very large settlements.

Its people grew wheat and barley, kept cattle and made pots painted with spirals in red, white and black, and clay figurines of women. Around 4000 BCE some villages in central Ukraine, such as Talianki and Maidanetske, grew to hundreds of hectares with perhaps 10,000 or more people, among the largest settlements on earth before the cities of Mesopotamia. Their houses were laid out in rings, and they burned them down from time to time, for reasons still debated. The culture faded as the climate changed and steppe herders spread. It is named after the villages of Cucuteni in Romania and Trypillia near Kyiv.
